summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics) with the harness assurance_generated_test.go; scratch removed. This turn opens a new line at the client-contract layer: question @node_propose_after_removal with a sourced Behaviour entry and an experiment, asking whether a proposal made through the Node API after the node applied its own removal reports that it cannot be admitted or simply blocks until the caller's context expires. Source trace: node.run's confc case applies the configuration and, when the node was a member before and is absent from the new voters, sets the proposal channel to nil with the comment 'If the node was removed, block incoming proposals' plus an explicit note that resetting it on leadership change 'isn't very sound and likely has bugs' (node.go:405-433), and Node.Propose reaches that channel through stepWithWaitOption, whose select can only complete on the channel, ctx.Done or n.done (node.go:513-537), so the raft layer's own drop signal (raft.go:1290-1295 for the removed-leader case) never appears on this path. The experiment drives one voter through the Node API while the other two are bare raft instances, measures the same Node.Propose call with the same 200 ms caller context before and after the node applies its own removal, and reports the operand pair used for the comparison (returned error text and elapsed time, with the derived blocked-until-deadline flag). Two comparisons encode the duty that an inadmissible proposal must be reported rather than merely timing out: the post-removal case (expected violated) and the member control (expected holds). Construction-time local runs show, for the record and not as formal evidence, that the control returns instantly with no error while the post-removal call blocks for the full timeout and returns only 'context deadline exceeded' with the node confirmed absent from voters [1,2]. Limitations record that a non-expiring caller context is not directly measured, that the removal is applied only on the subject node, and that embedding-service retry and timeout policies lie outside the captured package; the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained receipt.
